paradoxes.text: The switch bought a second patron, and the treaty capped it. The January 2024 move to Beijing was followed by a treaty that gives Australia an effective veto over any Chinese role in Nauru's security, banking and telecoms: the price of the new tie was a ceiling set by the old patron.

grand_strategy.reading: Nauru has a small economy, and its budget and its migration business come from Canberra; its one lever outside Australia is the seabed sponsorship, which waits on rules the International Seabed Authority has not written. The January 2024 switch from Taipei to Beijing shows that recognition is sold to whoever pays, but the December 2024 treaty capped the new patron by giving Australia a veto over security, banking and telecoms. Nauru therefore sells to several buyers while Canberra keeps the veto, and the Regional Processing Centre is at once its economy and its lever.

stances.note: Ally by treaty, not by defence. The December 2024 treaty gives Australia a say over Nauru's security, banking and telecommunications: no third-party engagement without Canberra's agreement. The ontology's own test for ally is a treaty, and the grade is Nauru's view of its own position, not Australia's. Australia's card reads the same treaty as partner ('not an alliance', no mutual defence); that is its reading of its side, and the two grades can differ. No source calls the relation reluctant, so reluctant ally is not used. Bond none: the tie is money and a veto, with no kinship, affinity or open grievance in the sources. Trend warming: the treaty was signed in December 2024 and the August 2025 memorandum extended it to the NZYQ cohort. Confidence B: one tier-2 and one tier-3 report of the treaty (ASPI, PINA), the treaty text not read; the 2025 memorandum rests on tier-3 press.

stances.note: Transactional. Nauru severed relations with Taipei on 15 January 2024 and restored them with Beijing on 24 January 2024 (the restoration date comes from a Wikipedia citation to Reuters, 25 January 2024, which was not opened). No treaty and no shared identity: the grade is partner, not reluctant partner, because no source read calls the relation reluctant. Trend stable: no further step after the switch is sourced, and the 2024 treaty caps Chinese engagement in security, banking and telecoms. Bond none. Confidence C: one tier-3 source, the same article the Taiwan card reads.
